title: Ground Supply Operations Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC I&L
raw_text:
3. MOS 3010, Ground Supply Operations Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC
I&L

    a. Summary. Ground Supply Operations Officers are technical experts who
are trained and appointed in writing to supervise and coordinate the
technical activities of a supply section of the operating forces or a shore
station organization. They may command or serve as a special staff officer.
They advise the commander on supply related matters and provide recommended
courses of action. They supervise and coordinate the technical aspects of
retail (using unit and intermediate) and wholesale-level supply activities in
the operating forces, supporting establishments, and with other supporting
agencies. They provide the technical knowledge of automated supply systems



                                         1-189                   Enclosure (1)
 1121                                                           NAVMC 1200.1L



necessary to ensure timely and accurate processing of supply related ADP
systems. They provide liaison between supply sections and supporting data
processing activities. They supervise supply chain management to include
procurement, receipt, inventory control (i.e. forecasting/stock
determination), storage, distribution, issue, disposal, and computation and
maintenance of stock positioning requirements. They supervise the
maintenance of subsistence, clothing, ammunition, and inventory control
accounts. Ground Supply Operations Officers assist in the budget execution,
fund justification, administration, and expenditure of allotted funds, and
make recommendations to the commanding officer regarding supply support
issues. They provide supply support insight for operational planning
requirements, supervise transportation of supplies and equipment, manage the
transmittal of public funds, participate in the budget process, administer,
and expend allotted funds, and make necessary recommendations to the
commanding officer regarding supply support procedures.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must have previously served in MOS 3047.

        (2) Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in
MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the Supply Chain Management Officer Course (M03C0G1),
MCB, Camp Lejeune, NC.

        (2) Complete the Intermediate Level Supply Operations Course
(M03SA21), MCB, Camp Lejeune, NC.

        (3) Complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4) within
18 months of appointment to WO.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (r), Ground Supply Training and Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Transportation, Storage, and Distribution Managers 11-3071.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
